clues.title: Language: Czech
text: Czech is a West Slavic language, mutually intelligible with Slovak. Czech and Slovak both use the special letters **Č, Ď, Ň, Š, Ť**, **Á, É, Í, Ó, Ú** and **Ý**. However, they both have some distinct letters that can be used to tell them apart:
Czech: **Ř, Ě** and **Ů**;
Slovak: **Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ** and **Ĺ**.

The Czech word for street is **ulice**, unlike ulica used in Slovak (and most other Slavic langauges). Most street signs in Czechia **don't include any** word meaning street, however. What you can learn instead is that if you see ulica, it will never be Czechia.
NOTE: Acute accents on vowels (**Á, É, Í, Ó, Ú** and **Ý**) are not found in South Slavic languages (Slovene, Serbo-Croatian).
